condition: Febrile infant under 3 months (NICE red feature)
permutationLabel: 7-week-old at a hernia review with fever, poor feeding and drowsiness (base case)
summary: 7-week-old girl (4.8 kg) attending the surgical clinic for review of a reducible umbilical hernia; fever 38.5 at home, feeding half the usual, sleepier; in clinic T 38.3, HR 178, RR 58, CRT 3 s. NICE NG143: age < 3 months with fever is a red feature — urgent paediatric assessment.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Umbilical hernia review — baby has a fever
inputs.hpi: 7-week-old girl booked for review of a small umbilical hernia. Mother reports a temperature of 38.5 °C at home this morning, taking about half her usual feeds and sleepier than normal. Fewer wet nappies. No vomiting, no cough, no rash. The hernia is unchanged and soft.

exam.general: Sleepy, wakes to handling, weak cry. T 38.3, HR 178, RR 58, SpO2 97%, CRT 3 s, mottled legs. Fontanelle flat.
exam.abdomen: Soft, 1 cm reducible umbilical hernia, non-tender.

inputs.socialHistory: Term baby, breastfed; 6-week immunisations due next week.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Fever in an infant under 3 months — serious bacterial infection to be excluded
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Febrile 7-week-old with red features (age < 3 months, reduced responsiveness, mottling). Same-day urgent paediatric assessment: FBC, CRP, blood culture, urine sample, consider lumbar puncture, parenteral antibiotics. Hernia review deferred.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE top 3: acute cholecystitis, GORD, peptic ulcer; PANE has UTI but nothing links fever in a young infant to it. Symptom inference ranks paediatric UTI #1 (secondary view).
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add a febrile-infant rule (NICE NG143): age < 3 months with T ≥ 38 °C → red feature.

emergencyLevel.note: Fever at < 3 months is a NICE red feature: same-day urgent paediatric assessment.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: No lumbar puncture suggested; the only infection output is the adult septic-shock bundle.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Febrile-infant rule (FBC, CRP, blood culture, urine, LP).

mustInclude.note: Graded as management because the engine lists the urine test inside a plan line.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: No paediatric referral: the output is the adult septic-shock bundle (meropenem, vasopressors 'if MAP < 65', urinary catheter, CT abdomen) — triggered by adult thresholds (SBP 78, HR 178 are labelled 'septic shock').
mustInclude.proposedFix: Febrile-infant rule → same-day urgent paediatric assessment; age-appropriate vital-sign ranges.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Only adult regimens (meropenem 1 g + vancomycin) are suggested; no cefotaxime/ceftriaxone ± amoxicillin for a young infant.

mustExclude.note: Weight 4.8 kg. Paracetamol 1 g, ibuprofen 400 mg, piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g, co-amoxiclav 1.2 g, meropenem 1 g, morphine 2.5–5 mg, ondansetron 4 mg and fixed 1 L, 1–2 L or 500 mL fluid volumes are adult fixed doses; a child needs weight-based (mg/kg, mL/kg) dosing. Prescribing accuracy is a patient-safety issue, so critical.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web: adult fixed doses with no weight or age adjustment — the hernia operative template's 'paracetamol 1g QDS + ibuprofen 400mg TDS', 'morphine 5mg PRN' and co-amoxiclav 1.2 g for a 4.8 kg infant.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Give protocol medications and prompt templates an age/weight branch (mg/kg and mL/kg with an adult maximum) and suppress fixed adult doses when age < 16 or weight < 50 kg; use age-specific vital-sign ranges before firing the adult shock/sepsis/tachycardia prompts.

mustExclude.note: The umbilical hernia is soft and reducible and the infant is febrile: any hernia operative plan today (let alone an adult laparoscopic inguinal TAPP with mesh, emergency or elective) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web: the hernia prompt now takes the elective branch (the 'non-tender' negation is fixed) but still produces a 'LAPAROSCOPIC INGUINAL HERNIA REPAIR (TAPP) — OPERATIVE PLAN' and 'Consent: hernia repair — … (TAPP), mesh infection, testicular ischaemia/vas injury' for a febrile 7-week-old's small reducible umbilical hernia.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Choose the hernia template by hernia type and age (no adult inguinal/mesh template for a paediatric umbilical hernia) and suppress operative templates while a sepsis/fever-in-infant prompt is active.

guideline.name: NICE NG143 — fever in under 5s: assessment and initial management
guideline.section: Age < 3 months with temperature ≥ 38 °C is a high-risk (red) feature; red features: refer for urgent paediatric assessment; infants < 3 months with fever: FBC, CRP, blood culture, urine testing, lumbar puncture in selected infants; parenteral antibiotics for infants 1–3 months with fever who appear unwell (and all < 1 month)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Fever in under 5s: assessment and initial management. NICE guideline NG143, 2019 (updated 2021).

rationale: A surgical clinic may be the first contact for a febrile young infant. Under 3 months, fever alone is high-risk: the hernia review stops and the infant goes for urgent paediatric assessment with a full septic screen.

authoring.author: Claude (prevention/screening, obstetric-gynaecological mimics and paediatric surgery cluster)
